quests.protocolRule: Think about what tells firefighters exactly where to search first.
quests.crisisScene: A house fire call comes in: parents say their baby is still inside upstairs, while they stand safely outside. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: GET THE BABY'S EXACT LOCATION IMMEDIATELY
quests.actionGuidance: An exact location lets firefighters go straight to the baby instead of searching the whole house room by room.

quests.protocolRule: Ask how firefighters might enter differently because of this.
quests.crisisScene: The parents say the baby's room is at the back of the house, the side the fire hasn't reached yet. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: PASS THIS ON, IT MAY CHANGE THE ENTRY POINT
quests.actionGuidance: Knowing the fire hasn't reached that side yet may let firefighters enter through a safer route to reach the baby faster.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what firefighters need to know isn't a risk here.
quests.crisisScene: A neighbor reports smoke from the same house but confirms no one else was home at the time. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: CONFIRM NO ONE ELSE IS INSIDE
quests.actionGuidance: Confirming no one else is inside lets firefighters focus entirely on reaching the baby without searching for anyone else.

quests.protocolRule: Ask which problem could affect his breathing, not just a limb.
quests.crisisScene: At a construction site, one worker has a broken arm and another has been exposed to fumes and is coughing hard. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: TREAT THE FUME EXPOSURE AS HIGHER PRIORITY
quests.actionGuidance: Fume exposure risks the airway and lungs, which is more urgent than a broken arm, even though the fracture looks more dramatic.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what a total loss of breath means compared to coughing.
quests.crisisScene: The coughing worker suddenly can't catch his breath at all. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: ESCALATE HIS CASE TO THE HIGHEST URGENCY
quests.actionGuidance: Being completely unable to breathe is immediately life-threatening, so this now becomes the single highest priority on the scene.

quests.protocolRule: Ask how this compares to a breathing emergency and a fracture.
quests.crisisScene: A third worker at the same site has only mild dust irritation in his eyes. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: TREAT THIS AS THE LOWEST PRIORITY HERE
quests.actionGuidance: Mild eye irritation is far less urgent than a breathing emergency or fracture, so it can wait until the others are handled.

quests.protocolRule: Ask whether either complaint has any warning signs attached.
quests.crisisScene: A woman reports a mild, familiar headache along with unrelated back pain from gardening. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: NEITHER NEEDS EMERGENCY SERVICES RIGHT NOW
quests.actionGuidance: A familiar mild headache and ordinary back pain are both non-urgent, so neither needs to be prioritized for emergency care.

quests.concept: On-Scene Evacuation Prior to Unit Arrival
quests.protocolRule: Ask which complaint no longer matches its usual pattern.
quests.crisisScene: The same woman's headache suddenly becomes the worst she's ever felt, unlike the back pain which hasn't changed. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: PRIORITIZE THE HEADACHE, IT HAS CHANGED CHARACTER
quests.actionGuidance: A sudden, severe change in a familiar headache is a warning sign, unlike the back pain which has stayed exactly the same.

quests.protocolRule: Is either complaint different from an ordinary day?
quests.crisisScene: A different caller has both mild back pain and a mild, familiar headache, with neither changing at all. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: RECOMMEND HER USUAL REMEDIES AND A DOCTOR'S VISIT IF EITHER LASTS
quests.actionGuidance: Both symptoms are mild and familiar, so routine remedies and a doctor's visit if either lasts are enough.

quests.protocolRule: Think about what's most useful even before injuries are known.
quests.crisisScene: A caller reports a multi-car pileup on a foggy highway but hasn't gotten out to check anyone yet. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: GET THE LOCATION FIRST, THEN ASK ABOUT INJURIES
quests.actionGuidance: Confirming the exact location first ensures responders are already moving, even while injury details are still being gathered.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what could happen to someone walking on a foggy highway.
quests.crisisScene: The caller then reports seeing at least one person moving between two of the wrecked cars. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: WARN THAT PERSON TO STAY OFF THE ROAD
quests.actionGuidance: Someone walking between wrecked cars on a foggy highway risks being hit by another vehicle, so they need an immediate warning.

quests.protocolRule: Ask whether this situation matches the danger of the pileup.
quests.crisisScene: A different caller reports a single stalled car on the highway shoulder, driver safely inside with hazards on. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT IT AS A LOW-PRIORITY BREAKDOWN
quests.actionGuidance: A safely stopped car with hazards on is a routine breakdown, not comparable in urgency to an active multi-car pileup.

quests.protocolRule: Has anything suddenly become dangerous?
quests.crisisScene: A caller reports a slow leak dripping from their ceiling that's gotten a little worse over the past week. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: ARRANGE A REPAIR AND PLACE A BUCKET UNDER THE LEAK
quests.actionGuidance: A slow, gradually worsening leak is a maintenance issue, not an emergency, since it hasn't created sudden danger.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what's different the moment it collapses.
quests.crisisScene: The same ceiling suddenly collapses, and part of it falls near where a child was playing. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: GET HELP NOW AND KEEP THE CHILD CLEAR OF THE COLLAPSED AREA
quests.actionGuidance: A sudden structural collapse near a child is now an emergency, even though the leak itself had built up slowly.

quests.protocolRule: Is it changing?
quests.crisisScene: A different caller reports a ceiling stain that has looked exactly the same for months. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: HAVE A ROOFER OR PLUMBER LOOK AT IT WHEN CONVENIENT
quests.actionGuidance: An unchanging stain with no progression isn't an emergency and can be handled through routine home repair.

quests.protocolRule: Ask which is more reliable here: his opinion or his memory test.
quests.crisisScene: A man insists he's 'totally fine' after a fall, but he can't remember what day it is. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: TRUST THE SYMPTOM, NOT HIS OWN ASSESSMENT
quests.actionGuidance: Confusion about the day is a concrete warning sign that outweighs his own claim of feeling fine after a fall.

quests.protocolRule: Ask whether recovering means the risk is completely gone.
quests.crisisScene: The same man then correctly answers several more questions and seems to be thinking clearly again. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REASSESS, BUT STILL RECOMMEND A CHECKUP
quests.actionGuidance: Recovering some clarity is reassuring, but a head injury still deserves a checkup, since confusion can return.

quests.concept: On-Scene Evacuation Prior to Unit Arrival
quests.protocolRule: Do his answers support his claim?
quests.crisisScene: A different caller after a minor bump confidently and consistently answers every question correctly. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: NO EMERGENCY, SUGGEST HE WATCH FOR HEADACHE OR DROWSINESS FOR A DAY
quests.actionGuidance: When someone's own claim of feeling fine matches consistent, clear answers, there's no conflicting evidence to override it.

quests.protocolRule: Ask whether either problem can simply wait for the other to finish.
quests.crisisScene: A kitchen fire has injured the cook with burns, and grease has spread flaming onto the floor. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REQUEST FIRE AND MEDICAL RESPONSE TOGETHER
quests.actionGuidance: Both the spreading fire and the burn injury need immediate, simultaneous responses, since neither can safely wait.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what matters more: the fire or his condition.
quests.crisisScene: The cook is now trying to put the fire out himself despite his burns. Input fire code!
quests.optimalResponse: TELL HIM TO GET OUT, NOT FIGHT THE FIRE
quests.actionGuidance: An injured person fighting a spreading fire risks worse harm, so getting him to safety matters more than saving the kitchen.

quests.protocolRule: Is the danger fully over just because the flames are gone?
quests.crisisScene: A small kitchen fire has been put out with a pot lid, but the oil pan is still smoking. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: LEAVE THE LID ON, TURN OFF THE HEAT, AND LET THE PAN COOL
quests.actionGuidance: Oil can reignite if the lid is lifted early. Keeping the lid on and the heat off lets it cool safely.

quests.protocolRule: Ask whose bones are more likely to be seriously hurt by the same fall.
quests.crisisScene: Two people fall on an icy sidewalk moments apart: a healthy young adult and an elderly man. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: CHECK THE ELDERLY MAN FIRST, THEN THE OTHER
quests.actionGuidance: An elderly person is generally more vulnerable to serious injury from the same kind of fall, so checking him first makes sense.

quests.protocolRule: Ask whether age still decides priority once there's a concrete injury.
quests.crisisScene: The young adult then says his wrist is bent at an unnatural angle. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: TREAT BOTH AS EQUAL PRIORITY NOW
quests.actionGuidance: A visibly deformed wrist is a clear, serious injury that now makes both cases equally urgent, regardless of age.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what factor would justify treating one before the other here.
quests.crisisScene: In a separate incident, two healthy adults of similar age both have minor bruises from a slip. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: CHECK THEM IN THE ORDER THEY ARRIVED, NEITHER NEEDS PRIORITY
quests.actionGuidance: With similar ages and similarly minor injuries, nothing justifies putting one person ahead of the other.

quests.protocolRule: Ask whether this detail changes what caused the crash.
quests.crisisScene: While reporting a car crash, the caller remembers the driver mentioned chest pain just before the crash happened. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: VOLUNTEER THIS DETAIL, EVEN IF NOT ASKED
quests.actionGuidance: Chest pain before the crash could mean a medical event caused it, which matters for how paramedics treat him.

quests.protocolRule: Would it change what responders do?
quests.crisisScene: The caller also remembers the driver's radio was playing loudly, which seems unrelated. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: LEAVE IT OUT OF THE REPORT
quests.actionGuidance: A loud radio has no bearing on his medical condition or the crash response, so it doesn't need to be passed on.

quests.protocolRule: Ask whether this detail helps explain what happened.
quests.crisisScene: A different caller remembers the crash happened right after the driver swerved to avoid a dog in the road. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: MENTION THE SWERVE, IT EXPLAINS THE CRASH
quests.actionGuidance: Mentioning the swerve gives responders a clearer picture of the crash, which can be useful, unlike the irrelevant radio detail.

quests.concept: On-Scene Evacuation Prior to Unit Arrival
quests.protocolRule: Ask whether either danger can be left out of the first report.
quests.crisisScene: A caller reports a collapsed scaffold at a construction site, with one worker pinned and another shouting that gas cylinders nearby have started hissing. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT THE GAS HAZARD AND THE PINNED WORKER TOGETHER
quests.actionGuidance: Both the pinned worker and the hissing gas need immediate attention, since one threatens him directly and the other threatens everyone nearby.

quests.protocolRule: Ask what needs to happen before anyone can safely reach the pinned worker.
quests.crisisScene: Responders ask which of the two problems needs the first team on scene. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: SEND THE HAZARD TEAM FIRST TO SECURE THE SCENE
quests.actionGuidance: Securing the gas hazard first makes it safe for rescuers to then reach and free the pinned worker without added risk.

quests.protocolRule: Ask whether these two calls deserve the same amount of urgency.
quests.crisisScene: A second, unrelated call reports a minor two-car fender bender with no injuries, in a different part of town. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: TREAT THIS AS FAR LOWER PRIORITY
quests.actionGuidance: A minor fender-bender with no injuries is far less urgent than an active multi-hazard rescue and can wait for available responders.
